additional_info: Founded through the vision and donation of Dimitar A. Tsenov, the academy has played an important role in the identity of Svishtov for nearly a century. Thousands of students from across Bulgaria have passed through its halls, making the city not only a historical destination, but also a place shaped by education and academic life.

name: Danube Riverside Area
why_and_how_it_will_work:

additional_info: The Danube riverside is one of the places where the atmosphere of Svishtov can really be felt. It connects the city with the river that shaped its trade, history, and everyday life for generations, while today it offers space for walking, relaxation, family activities, and local events. If you’d like to continue your trip across the Danube, the easiest way is through the bridge near Ruse or the ferry crossing at Oryahovo. Even today, the river keeps Svishtov connected with the towns and cultures on the Romanian side of the Danube.

additional_info: Holy Trinity Church is one of the buildings connected to the famous Bulgarian builder Kolyu Ficheto. His work can still be seen in different parts of Bulgaria today, and many people visit Svishtov especially to see one of his churches up close and learn more about the master behind some of the country’s most recognizable buildings

additional_info: Just outside Svishtov are the remains of Novae — one of the most important Roman military camps along the Danube. Nearly two thousand years ago, Roman soldiers, merchants, and travelers passed through this area, turning it into an important part of the empire’s northern border. Today, visitors can still walk among the ruins and get a glimpse of what life here may have looked like centuries ago.

name: Kaleto Fortress
additional_info: “Kaleto is one of the places locals usually recommend for the view over the Danube. People come here mostly in the evening — for the sunset, the fresh air, and the feeling of seeing the whole city from above.”

name: Park Kaleto & Sun Dial
additional_info: “The park around Kaleto is one of the most popular places for walks in Svishtov. The sun dial is one of those small details many visitors stop to look at, especially when they hear it has become a recognizable part of the park.”

name: Memorial Park Pametnicite
additional_info: “Pametnicite is connected to the crossing of the Russian troops over the Danube during the Russo-Turkish War. Today the area is quiet, but many people visit because of the monuments, the river view, and the connection to an important moment in Bulgarian history.”

name: Metoch “Sts Peter and Paul”
additional_info: “The Metoch is one of the quieter historical places in the city. Besides being connected to religious life, places like this were also important during the Bulgarian Revival period, when education and community life often happened around churches and monasteries.”

name: Pokrov Bogorodichen Monastery
additional_info: “The monastery is hidden in the forest outside Svishtov and many locals visit it because of the peaceful atmosphere around it. The road to the monastery passes through trees and nature, which makes the place feel very different from the city itself.”

name: Clock Tower of Svishtov
additional_info:
“The clock tower is one of the old symbols of Svishtov. Long before phones and watches, towers like this helped people organize daily life and became natural meeting points in the town.”                                     “The Clock Tower is one of the old symbols of Svishtov and stands near what was once the city’s busy торговски area. It was built in 1763 by master builder Bogdan, at a time when clock towers were much more than landmarks — they helped people organize daily life and were an important part of Danube trading towns.”
“It is believed that the tower was built for the needs of the merchants and craftsmen of Svishtov, and marble plaques with old inscriptions can still be seen on the building today.”

“In 1890, a new clock mechanism made in Austria was installed in the tower. For decades, the sound of the clock was part of the everyday rhythm of the city.”

“Today, many visitors pass by the tower without noticing it, but for local people it remains part of the old atmosphere and identity of Svishtov.”
